properties.Location: South Side of Santa Rosa Island, Between Ford Point and South Point
properties.IncidentOverview: On Friday; May 15; 2026; an aircraft flying over Santa Rosa Island in Channel Islands National Park reported a wildfire. National Park Service (NPS) staff already on the island confirmed it later that morning. The Santa Rosa Island Fire is located on the southeastern end of the island in remote and rugged terrain. The National Weather Service has issued a Gale Warning until 3 AM on Monday; May 18. This is a full-suppression human-caused wildfire and is under investigation. Current Situation: The fire remains active on the eastern and western edges / flanks. On the east side; the fire has reached East Point and the East Point Road. On the west side; fire activity has moderated and the fire remains in the area of the South Point Lighthouse. The status of the lighthouse is unknown. Dozens of firefighters and rangers remain on the island. Crews are working today to go direct where possible and safe to do so in areas with the highest probability of success; especially to help protect park infrastructure and values at risk. It’s important to note that firefighters are working closely with Channel Islands National Park staff to ensure the protection of cultural assets and sites; along with the island’s unique plant and animal habitat. Six plant species are found on Santa Rosa Island and nowhere else in the world. Firefighters are also working on an indirect containment strategy if the fire reaches Clapp Spring to protect the main historic and operational area of the island. This includes working north of the fire along the Telephone Road. Additional fire crews are on order and expected to be transported out to the island tomorrow after the winds subside and boating conditions are safer. Closures: The National Park Service has closed Santa Rosa Island to day use and overnight use at least through this week due to the wildfire. Visitors with campground reservations at Water Canyon Campground have been notified via e-mail. Structures: There are two uninhabited historic structures in the area; Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed on the western edge; and Wreck Line Camp Cabin on the eastern edge. Unfortunately; both have been confirmed destroyed. An additional storage structure was also destroyed adjacent to Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed.
